People / community

Suquamish

Suquamish histories center on the waterways of central Puget Sound and on Lushootseed-speaking village life. The Tribe and its museum explain both the disruption of communal places and continuing work to sustain community gathering.

Read the sources [1] Suquamish Tribe [2] suquamishmuseum.org [3] Suquamish Museum / Suquamish Tribe

03

Villages and seasonal waterways

The Tribe describes permanent winter villages near shorelines and seasonal travel by family canoes to fishing, hunting and gathering places. Its account connects Suquamish with other communities through language, relationships and exchange. This reading introduces those connections without turning a historical village list into present government boundaries.

Read the sources [1] Suquamish Tribe

04

A place for community gathering

The museum dates the dedication of the House of Awakened Culture to 2009 and explains it as a response to the loss of communal gathering space associated with Old Man House. It describes the building as a setting for community and intertribal events. Read this as a public institutional account; its artwork and ceremonies have separate permissions.

Read the sources [3] Suquamish Museum / Suquamish Tribe
